Words2Numbers.__init__:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Initialize number-word parsing state by building lookup tables for cardinal words, scale words, irregular ordinal words, and ordinal suffix rewrite rules." __init__]
    [INPUTS]
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Initialize self.numwords as an empty dictionary to store number-word mappings. RESULT self.numwords]
            [COMMAND Assign self.units to the ordered list of unit number words from zero through nineteen. RESULT self.units]
            [COMMAND Assign self.tens to the ordered list of tens words with empty string placeholders at indices 0 and 1, followed by twenty through ninety. RESULT self.tens]
            [COMMAND Assign self.scales to the ordered list of scale words hundred, thousand, million, billion, and trillion. RESULT self.scales]
            [COMMAND Insert the fixed mapping in self.numwords for the key "and" with the tuple value (1, 0). RESULT self.numwords]
            [COMMAND Iterate over enumerate(self.units), and for each idx and word, assign self.numwords[word] to the tuple (1, idx). RESULT self.numwords]
            [COMMAND Iterate over enumerate(self.tens), and for each idx and word, assign self.numwords[word] to the tuple (1, idx * 10), including the empty string entries at indices 0 and 1 which map to (1, 0) and (1, 10). RESULT self.numwords]
            [COMMAND Iterate over enumerate(self.scales), and for each idx and word, assign self.numwords[word] to the tuple (10 ** (idx * 3 or 2), 0), producing hundred -> (100, 0), thousand -> (1000, 0), million -> (1000000, 0), billion -> (1000000000, 0), and trillion -> (1000000000000, 0). RESULT self.numwords]
            [COMMAND Assign self.ordinal_words to the dictionary of irregular ordinal word mappings: first to 1, second to 2, third to 3, fifth to 5, eighth to 8, ninth to 9, and twelfth to 12. RESULT self.ordinal_words]
            [COMMAND Assign self.ordinal_endings to the ordered list of suffix rewrite rules [('ieth', 'y'), ('th', '')], preserving rule order for later matching behavior. RESULT self.ordinal_endings]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
Words2Numbers.text2int:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Convert number and ordinal words embedded in input text into their numeric string forms while preserving non-numeric words and token boundaries." text2int]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> textnum </REF>: string "Input text that may contain hyphenated words, number words, ordinal words, and ordinary non-numeric words."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> curstring </REF>: string "A transformed string where recognized numeric word sequences are replaced with their numeric values and other words are preserved with spacing behavior matching the method."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Normalize the input text by replacing every '-' character in textnum with a single space and store the result back into textnum. RESULT textnum]
            [COMMAND Initialize current to 0, result to 0, curstring to an empty string, and onnumber to False before token processing begins. RESULT current,result,curstring,onnumber]
            [COMMAND Split textnum on whitespace and iterate over each token in order as word. RESULT word]
            [COMMAND Within the loop for each word, if word exists in self.ordinal_words, set scale to 1 and increment to self.ordinal_words[word], update current to current * scale + increment, and set onnumber to True. RESULT scale,increment,current,onnumber]
            [COMMAND Within the loop for each word, if word does not exist in self.ordinal_words, iterate through every pair ending and replacement in self.ordinal_endings and, for each pair where word.endswith(ending) is True, rewrite word as word without its last len(ending) characters followed by replacement; do not stop after a match. RESULT word]
            [COMMAND Still within the non-direct-ordinal branch, if the possibly rewritten word is not present in self.numwords, then if onnumber is True append repr(result + current) followed by a single space to curstring, append word followed by a single space to curstring, reset result to 0 and current to 0, and set onnumber to False. RESULT curstring,result,current,onnumber]
            [COMMAND Still within the non-direct-ordinal branch, if the possibly rewritten word is present in self.numwords, read scale and increment from self.numwords[word], update current to current * scale + increment, and if scale > 100 then add current to result and reset current to 0; after that set onnumber to True. RESULT scale,increment,current,result,onnumber]
            [COMMAND After the loop finishes, if onnumber is True, append repr(result + current) to curstring without adding a trailing space. RESULT curstring]
            [COMMAND Return curstring. RESULT return]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: During token processing, the current token is not a recognized direct ordinal word and remains absent from self.numwords after all ordinal ending rewrites.]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND If a numeric phrase is currently in progress because onnumber is True, flush the accumulated numeric value by appending repr(result + current) and a trailing space to curstring. RESULT curstring]
            [COMMAND Append the non-numeric word and a trailing space to curstring. RESULT curstring]
            [COMMAND Reset numeric accumulation state by setting result to 0, current to 0, and onnumber to False. RESULT result,current,onnumber]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: During token processing, the current token is a recognized direct ordinal word in self.ordinal_words.]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Treat the token as an ordinal numeric increment by using scale 1 and increment self.ordinal_words[word], then update current to current * 1 + increment. RESULT current]
            [COMMAND Mark that numeric parsing is active by setting onnumber to True. RESULT onnumber]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: During token processing, the current token is found in self.numwords after any ordinal ending rewrites.]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Load scale and increment from self.numwords[word] and update current to current * scale + increment. RESULT scale,increment,current]
            [COMMAND If scale > 100, fold the accumulated current into result by setting result to result + current and then reset current to 0. RESULT result,current]
            [COMMAND Mark that numeric parsing is active by setting onnumber to True. RESULT onnumber]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
Words2Numbers.is_valid_input:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Validates that a text input contains only recognized numeric or ordinal words after normalizing hyphens to spaces and converting ordinal suffixes when needed." is_valid_input]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> textnum </REF>: string "The input text to validate as a sequence of numeric or ordinal words."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: boolean "Returns true if every whitespace-separated word is either a recognized ordinal word or can be normalized into a recognized numeric word; otherwise returns false."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Replace every '-' character in textnum with a space character and store the normalized string back into textnum. RESULT textnum]
            [COMMAND Iterate over each whitespace-separated word produced by splitting textnum. RESULT word_iteration]
            [COMMAND Within the loop for each word, if the word exists in self.ordinal_words, skip all remaining processing for that word and continue to the next word. RESULT next_word_if_ordinal]
            [COMMAND Within the loop for each word that is not in self.ordinal_words, iterate over each ending and replacement pair in self.ordinal_endings. RESULT ordinal_ending_iteration]
            [COMMAND Within the inner loop, if the current word ends with the current ending, update word to word without its last len(ending) characters followed by replacement using the format "%s%s". RESULT word]
            [COMMAND After completing the inner ordinal ending loop for a non-ordinal word, check whether the resulting word is absent from self.numwords. RESULT word_membership_check]
            [COMMAND If the resulting word is not in self.numwords, return false immediately and stop all further processing. RESULT False]
            [COMMAND If all words finish processing without triggering the false return, return true. RESULT True]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: A processed word is not already in self.ordinal_words and, after all ordinal ending replacements have been attempted, the resulting word is still not in self.numwords.]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return false immediately without processing any remaining words. RESULT False]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
